statement: Let κ be the number of cylin- drical ends. The observations can be chosen so that their values are q = P(p) in analytic reduced coordinates p = (b, x) ∈ Rm−κ × Rκ, with the following properties. (1) At x = 0 there is a real analytic family Sb of normalized solutions of (3.4). It has the same end types as S, permits independent end tilts, and permits changes of its conical links within the normalized family. Outside the fixed observation support it is an exact shrinker. Its cylindrical remainder after rotating the end is O(z−2+η) for every fixed η > 0, on a parameter neighborhood that may depend on this choice. On each conical end its link graph satisfies vb(t, θ) = vb,∞(θ) + O(e−2t ) (3.26) in every fixed log and angular derivative, with vb,∞ analytic in b. These bounds and their fixed parameter derivatives are uniform on a closed small parameter ball. (2) There is a unique formal normalized solution in x, u(b, x) ∼ ∑ α∈Nκ uα(b)xα , λ(b, x) ∼ ∑ α λα(b)xα , based at Sb, whose coefficients in the prescribed graph charts have polynomial growth and are analytic in b. For real b, their coefficientwise conversions to normal graph jets are smooth in b and have uniform polynomial bounds at every fixed derivative order. After removal of the first-order tilt, the term homogeneous of degree one in x on cylindrical end j is √ 2 2 βj(b, x)z2 + O(|x|zη ), β(b, x) = M(b)x, (3.27) where M(b) is an analytic invertible κ×κ matrix. In particular β is exactly homogeneous linear in x for fixed b. 20 OPENAI (3) Integrating the Gaussian action coefficient by coefficient defines F ∈ R{b}[[x]], with ∇pF = (DpP)T λ. (3.28) Every fixed truncation of the prescribed graph series and every fixed number of its pa- rameter or spatial derivatives has uniform polynomial end bounds on a sufficiently small complex b neighborhood. The real normal truncations have the analogous smooth bounds for real parameters. This neighborhood may depend on the fixed truncation and deriva- tive orders. When the limiting links and cylindrical directions are separated, as for the tangent section in Theorem 2.2, the real family on a closed sufficiently small ball has the following additional geometry. Its smooth rescaled conical annuli, the rotated cylindrical tails, and the compact core have uniform bounded geometry. There is a uniform positive normal tubular radius; on a sufficiently far conical annulus of radius r the tubular radius is at least cr. In the prescribed parametrizations |∂bXb| ≤ C(1 + |X|) and its physical first derivative is bounded. These statements concern the real surfaces; complex parameter continuation is taken in the prescribed coordinates on a fixed real atlas.
